title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page finishes a sentence begun on the previous page, the Remarque after formula (324). That page sets up a commutative group scheme J°_{U/S} over a base S, with a distinguished section e ∈ H^0(S, J°_{U/S}), which it glosses as the original 'elliptic Jacobian'. Here J°_{U/S} is presumably the connected (generalized) Jacobian attached to a punctured curve U/S, with compactification an elliptic curve X̃/S. Throughout, T_∞ denotes the full Tate module, the limit over n of the n-torsion J°[n]. The Kummer coboundary (324), H^0(S, J°) → H^1(S, T_∞(J°)), sends e to the class of the torsor F_∞ of its compatible systems of division points e/n. Its kernel is the subgroup of infinitely divisible sections. For S reduced and of finite type over Z this kernel is zero, which Grothendieck calls 'elementary'. This page completes the conclusion: the distinguished section e is entirely determined once one knows two things. (1°) The étale covers S' → S corresponding to the points of order 2 of X̃/S, i.e. the S-scheme X̃[2] of 2-torsion points. In a Legendre-type picture these are the branch points of X̃ → P^1, so their positions are what define the punctures of U and hence the toric part of the generalized Jacobian. This yields an identification J°_{U/S} ≃ J°(X̃, S'), the generalized Jacobian of X̃ with modulus supported on S'. (2°) The T_∞(J°)-torsor F_∞(X̃/S) of division points of e. In modern terms this is the injectivity of the Kummer map for a (semi-)abelian scheme over an arithmetic base. It is used to recover a geometric datum (the point e) from purely étale / Galois-theoretic data. That fits the surrounding programme: describing M_{1,1} → Out-type groups and the 'interpretation of Π_Q → N_σ' in section 15°, the anabelian reconstruction of the Galois action on the profinite π_1 of M_{1,1} and M_{0,3}.
errors: The vanishing of the kernel needs justification, which the text only calls 'elementary'. A correct elementary argument: an infinitely divisible section stays infinitely divisible at every closed point s. There J°(k(s)) is a finite group, since k(s) is a finite field, so the section vanishes at every closed point. S is reduced and of finite type over Z, hence Jacobson, so the section vanishes. This uses separatedness/flatness of J° over S, which is presumably implicit. So the claim is fine, and does not need Mordell–Weil / Lang–Néron.
The isomorphism written after 'd'où' is partly illegible and its exact form (generalized Jacobian with modulus S') cannot be verified from the page alone.

ideas.what: A section of a (semi-)abelian scheme over a reduced base of finite type over Z is determined by its Kummer class in H^1(S, T_∞). The kernel of the Kummer map consists of infinitely divisible sections, and these vanish.
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of the Kummer map / no nonzero divisible points over finitely generated bases
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Kummer theory; Lang–Néron, Mordell–Weil); standard in anabelian-geometry literature
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) discusses analogous injectivity for the section conjecture; not this specific statement

ideas.what: Recovering the 'elliptic' section e from two pieces of étale data: the 2-torsion étale cover (which fixes the punctures and the generalized Jacobian) and the division-point torsor F_∞.
ideas.modern_name: Galois-theoretic reconstruction of points via Kummer torsors (anabelian flavour)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Anabelian geometry (Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki) for analogous reconstructions
ideas.where_published: Context of La Longue Marche (1981), unpublished notes

deep.surprise_reason: A short conclusion of a standard Kummer-injectivity remark inside the Longue Marche computations. The content is routine, and the subsequent anabelian literature contains equivalent statements.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'd'où π^0_{S'}π^0_{U/S} ≃ π^0(X̃,S')' is more plausibly 'd'où J°_{U/S} ≃ J°_?(X̃, S')' (a generalized Jacobian of X̃ with modulus S'). The symbols are J-like, not π, and the subscript before (X̃, S') is struck out.
Line 3: 'T_∞(π_{...})' should read 'T_∞(J°_{...})' with a struck-out subscript; the object is the T_∞(J°)-torsor F_∞(X̃/S).
Line 1: 'associés correspondants' — the first word appears to be a deletion; read 'Les revêtements étales S' de S associés, correspondant aux pts d'ordre 2 de X̃/S'.
